title: Lost phone, MFA no longer works
symptom: User lost her phone and cannot approve sign-ins
user_description: I lost my phone and I need it to sign in. I can't get into anything and I have deadlines today.

options.text: Turn off MFA on her account so she can sign in
options.why: Removes a key protection and could let an attacker in, especially since her phone is lost.

options.text: Reset MFA for anyone who asks over the phone
options.why: Anyone could pretend to be her. Identity must be checked first.

options.text: Verify her identity using the approved process, reset and re-register her MFA method, and report the lost phone to security if it could access work data
options.why: Strong identity checks stop attackers using a 'lost phone' story. A lost phone with work access should be reported so security can protect the account and data.

options.text: Tell her to wait until she finds the phone
options.why: Leaves her unable to work and does nothing about a possible security risk.

hints: Why is a request to reset MFA a favourite trick for attackers?
How do you confirm it is really her?
Could the lost phone be a security risk?
real_world_tip: If the phone was lost, ask whether it had a lock screen. This tells security how worried to be.
